questions.question: What is a closure in JavaScript?
questions.title: Closures in JavaScript
questions.direct_answer: A closure is a function bundled with references to variables from its lexical outer scope. It can continue to read or update those variables after the outer function has returned, which enables factories, private state, and callbacks.

sections.title: Remember
items: Closures capture lexical bindings, not a frozen snapshot.
They are common in callbacks, factories, and module patterns.
Remove unnecessary listeners to avoid retaining captured objects.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content: A closure is a function with access to variables from its lexical outer scope. That scope stays alive while the function is reachable, which is why closures are useful for private state and callbacks but can retain memory if listeners are never cleaned up.

sections.title: Build the mental model
sections.content:
A closure is a function bundled with references to variables from its lexical outer scope.

It can continue to read or update those variables after the outer function has returned, which enables factories, private state, and callbacks.

A closure keeps access to the lexical environment where it was created. The outer function may finish, but the captured binding remains reachable through the inner function.
